title: Palenque
summary: Palenque, in Chiapas, Mexico, was a Classic Maya capital known for refined architecture and sculpted reliefs. It rose to regional power around 500 CE and was ruled in the seventh century by K'inich Janaab' Pakal, whose tomb lies inside the Temple of the Inscriptions. The city was abandoned around the ninth century.

uncertainty.note: INAH's site card gives 400-900 AD; UNESCO says the city was founded in the Late Preclassic, became a powerful capital around AD 500, and was abandoned about the 9th century.
